ref exposed via forwardRef (mirrors Svelte's ref = $bindable(null))

Timestamp clock: the Svelte root builds a private createNow() and only starts it inside $effect while a valid timestamp is shown. React calls useNow() unconditionally (a hook cannot be conditional), so a ChatMessage rendered without a `timestamp` also joins the shared clock. Net cost is lower, not higher — useNow is one page-wide interval shared by every consumer, where the Svelte side paid one interval per message — and it still stops when the last consumer unmounts (asserted by the 'stops ticking once unmounted' test).

The snippet props (`avatar`, `actions`, `footer`, `children`) are ReactNode and are rendered on truthiness, so a deliberately falsy node (0, "", false) renders nothing where Svelte's `{#if snippet}` could never receive one.

SSR relative timestamps: Svelte's `createNow` seeds itself with `Date.now()` at construction, so its server HTML carries real relative labels. React's shared clock cannot — the hydration render has no way to reproduce the server's timestamp, and sampling the wall clock on a render path breaks convention C-7 — so `useNow()` returns a `NaN` sentinel until the clock is retained in the layout phase, and `formatRelativeTime` renders a non-finite `now` as `""`. The server HTML therefore ships an empty label (never a wrong one) and it fills in before the first paint. Pinned by `react/src/internals/use-elapsed.ssr.test.ts`.

minors.problem: `const body = children ?? <StreamingText .../>` uses nullish coalescing where the Svelte source gates on truthiness (`{#if children}`). A children node that is `false`, `""` or `0` (e.g. `{cond && <X/>}`) suppresses the StreamingText fallback and renders an empty body, whereas Svelte would render the content. The port's divergence note also mis-describes this as 'rendered on truthiness'.

`useNow()` is called unconditionally, so a ChatMessage rendered without a `timestamp` still retains the shared 30s clock, where the Svelte root's `$effect(() => isValidTime ? now.start() : undefined)` started no interval at all. Declared as a divergence and mitigated by the clock being page-wide and released on the last unmount, so net cost is lower than Svelte's per-message interval.

`ref = $bindable(null)` becomes `forwardRef`, delivering the native `<input>` element through the standard React ref channel.

`class` -> `className`; the Svelte `ref = $bindable(null)` becomes `forwardRef`, so `<Combobox ref={...} />` yields the `<input>` element.

React portals bubble SYNTHETIC events through the React tree where a Svelte-moved node's native events stop at `<body>` (inherited contract divergence D-1; inert in practice — `useDismissable` listens natively on `document`).

`class` prop becomes `className` (package-wide convention).
`ref = $bindable(null)` becomes `forwardRef<HTMLButtonElement | HTMLAnchorElement, CopyButtonProps>`, forwarded to the inner Button exactly as the Svelte source does.

Declared as a divergence by the port and consistent with the Meteors/FallingStarsBg precedent in this campaign; behaviour on first mount is identical.

divergences: Adds a `seed` prop (default 1) with a deterministic mulberry32 PRNG replacing the source's Math.random() — required for identical server render and hydration; same seed yields the same initial field.
Sparkle ids drop the source's Date.now()+Math.random() composition in favor of an extra PRNG draw (`${x}-${y}-${random()}`) — ids stay unique per field but are deterministic.
Post-mount star regeneration draws from a second seeded stream (mulberry32(seed+1)) instead of Math.random(), so the animation timeline is also deterministic per seed.

No two-way binding in React: Svelte's `state = $bindable("idle")` becomes a plain `state` prop plus a new `onStateChange?: (state) => void` callback that fires when StatusMorph itself writes back to "idle" via the resetAfter timer. Callers who want the auto-reset to actually change what they render must wire onStateChange into their own state, unlike the Svelte bind:state contract which mutates the caller's variable automatically.
`ref = $bindable(null)` on the Svelte side is a forwardRef in React per PORTING.md C-4; no other ref-related behavior differs.

The Svelte StatusMorphHarness.test.svelte is not a separate file in the port — its role is filled by an inline Harness function component defined at the top of StatusMorph.test.tsx (React has no equivalent of importing a `.test.svelte` rig from a `.test.ts` file), so the matrix's two listed test files collapse into one .test.tsx, as instructed.

`STEPPER_KEY` is a `React.Context<StepperContext | undefined>` object, not a `Symbol` context key — read with `useContext(STEPPER_KEY)`. Same exported name, same optional-outside-the-root semantics (button-group's `BUTTON_GROUP_CONTEXT_KEY` precedent).

minors.problem: Controlled/uncontrolled pair semantics differ from `$bindable` in one edge case: a consumer that passes `current` but no `onCurrentChange` gets a stepper that never moves on click, whereas the Svelte side's `current = index` assignment (Stepper.svelte:78) updates the component's own copy and visibly advances even when the prop is not bound. This is the sanctioned React idiom for `bind:`, is the pattern used across this port, and was declared as divergence #1 — recorded for completeness, not as a defect.

divergences: activeIndex is controlled-when-passed (tabs precedent for `$bindable`): omit it for uncontrolled use; when passed, the parent must echo `onChange` back for internal activations (IO/focus) to take effect — Svelte's unbound-prop local-override semantics have no React counterpart.
`item`/`panel` snippets become render-prop functions `(item, index, active) => ReactNode` / `(item, index) => ReactNode`, per PORTING.md snippet mapping.

The `{#key panelIndex}` crossfade is rebuilt on usePresence + preset("fade") (per internals-api.md §5.1 row 1); an exiting frame freezes the panel content from the render BEFORE the index changed (the counterpart of Svelte freezing the outgoing keyed block's DOM), so during the one render where the swap is detected the still-live frame briefly shows the new index's content — invisible in practice (same commit, pre-paint swap).
Exiting frames are marked `inert` by usePresence's default, matching Svelte's own outroing-block inert marking.
`children` is omitted from the rest-prop attribute surface: the Svelte source renders no children snippet, and a React children spread onto the root div would render where Svelte rendered nothing.

A panel frame interrupted mid-entrance reverses from its current opacity over a proportionally shortened duration rather than snapping back to full and restarting the fade, because `usePresence` owns one bidirectional leg per node where the Svelte source used a split `in:`/`out:` pair.

`StickyScroll`'s exported type is restored by assertion, because forwardRef erases a render function's type parameter and ref-as-prop is React-19-only while the peer range includes 18; the same idiom restores the type parameter on the memoised internal row.

minors.problem: If items shrinks to an empty array while a panel crossfade is in flight, the render-phase frame-push logic still queues a new frame entry (panelIndex is computed as 0 even for empty items), which never mounts since the panel wrapper isn't rendered when items.length===0. It sits inertly in the frames state array (harmless — renders null if it ever mounts later) rather than being pruned. Not covered by any test on either side; not a visible/functional regression from the Svelte source's own behavior in this scenario.

divergences: onComplete edge-detection runs in a useEffect (post-commit) rather than Svelte's untracked $effect body — observably equivalent (fires once on the true→false edge, never on mount), but React fires it after paint instead of synchronously during the reactive flush.

minors.problem: Root class list order differs from the Svelte source: Svelte's cn("ft-subagents w-full text-sm", className) plus a class:ft-subagents-compact directive puts the compact class after the caller's className; the React port's cn("ft-subagents w-full text-sm", compact && "ft-subagents-compact", className) puts it before. No competing same-specificity rule depends on this order, so there is no visual/functional difference — purely cosmetic.

divergences: Switch: Svelte `bind:checked` becomes the standard controlled/uncontrolled split — uncontrolled by default with a new `defaultChecked` prop, controlled when `checked` is passed (pair with `onCheckedChange`).

TabsTrigger: the focus reclaim waits for `focusedValue` to stop naming this trigger before acting, because React lands the unregister state update one render after the commit that disabled the button, where Svelte's cleanup has already completed by the time its effect body runs. Same observable behaviour; the flag is now consumed on the empty-registry answer too, so no reclaim can survive into a later re-enable.

TabsTrigger: the `document.activeElement` sample is kept continuously by `handleFocus`/`handleBlur` (plus an activeElement read in the layout effect) because React has no pre-mutation phase equivalent to `$effect.pre`. Pre-existing in the port; unchanged by this fix.

`TABS_KEY` is a `React.Context<TabsContext | undefined>` object (displayName "TabsContext") rather than the Svelte `unique symbol` context key — read it with `useContext(TABS_KEY)`. `TabsContext`'s `value`, `orientation`, `activation`, `variant` and `focusedValue` are plain readonly fields on an object the root rebuilds every render, not Svelte getters.

minors.problem: The `value` prop is strictly controlled (passing it without an `onValueChange` that writes back freezes the selection), whereas Svelte's `value = $bindable("")` still writes its own local copy when passed without `bind:`. This is the unavoidable rune-to-React gap and matches the house pattern already shipped in ToggleGroup and Stepper, and it is documented in the prop's JSDoc — but it is a real API-surface divergence and was not listed in the port agent's divergences report.

Root class gains a port-added `terminal-text` anchor token (sanctioned by PORTING.md styling rule 2: the Svelte <style> was compiler-scoped with no root class; `.cursor-blink` is anchored under it, keyframe name `blink` kept identical).
The stream restarts on `lines` CONTENT change, not on array identity: a re-allocated equal-content array keeps the current stream running, where the Svelte side restarts it.
`class` prop becomes `className` (standard React rename per PORTING.md).
Trailing ` ` after each word is rendered as the JSX string literal `" "` — identical character in the DOM.

TextRevealStars takes a `seed?: number` prop (default 1) with a deterministic mulberry32 PRNG in place of Math.random() in the render path (SSR/hydration safety, per PORTING.md seed rule); same seed = same star field, call order matches the Svelte generator.
TextRevealCard takes a `starsSeed?: number` prop forwarded to the star field so card consumers can vary the layout (the Svelte side reshuffles randomly per mount).

Port-added CSS anchor class `text-reveal-stars` on the stars root div: the Svelte compiler scoped `.star-animate { animation: star-drift ... }` and the source has no root class, so the rule is anchored as `.text-reveal-stars .star-animate` to avoid leaking the generic name; keyframe name `star-drift` unchanged.

touchmove is attached natively via useEffect with { passive: false } instead of React's onTouchMove: the handler calls preventDefault() and React registers its touchmove root listener as passive. Same listener semantics as the Svelte attribute; behavior identical.

Mid-roll DOM order inside the aria-hidden cell layer: exiting cells are appended after the current cells instead of holding their original sibling position (explicit grid-column/grid-row placement makes the painted result identical; only DOM inspection during the roll window can tell)

On a length-changing update the generation bump lands in a post-commit effect (mirroring the source's after-DOM-update $effect), so one committed frame may briefly reuse a positionally-matching node before the full re-roll — same two-phase behavior as Svelte, but the intermediate frame is a real React commit

rollIn/rollOut return the package's local TransitionSpec (delay always present) instead of svelte/transition's TransitionConfig — visible only to direct importers of roll-transitions.ts, which neither package exports from its index

On a `direction="auto"` reversal both legs of the same roll travel the same way, because the port resolves the direction before the leg orchestrator runs; the reference starts the outro with the previous direction, so its two glyphs cross.

A grapheme whose key returns while its old cell is still rolling out eases back from wherever the exit leg had got to, because the shared transition sampler hands the in-flight run to the reversing leg as its counterpart; the reference replays the whole entrance from fully hidden.

minors.problem: Effect 2 (generation bump + backstop) runs in a plain useEffect (post-paint, macrotask-scheduled), whereas Svelte's equivalent $effect runs as a pre-paint microtask. On a length-changing update this means React can commit-and-paint one real frame using the stale (pre-bump) generation — where mergeCells treats an accidentally position-matching cell as unchanged instead of forcing the full re-roll — before a second effect-triggered render corrects it to the full reroll a moment later. Svelte never paints that intermediate frame. The port agent disclosed this accurately in notes, it follows PORTING.md's mandated $effect→useEffect mapping (deviating to a layout effect here was a considered option they rejected), and the corresponding test ("replaces every cell on a length change...") already uses waitFor to accommodate the eventual-consistency timing rather than asserting synchronously — so this is a known, defensible, self-correcting edge case rather than a silent bug.

Exiting cells inside the aria-hidden cell layer are appended after all current cells in mergeCells (rather than holding their original sibling index), diverging from Svelte's keyed-each DOM ordering during the roll window. Confirmed harmless: every cell is explicitly placed via inline grid-column-start plus a shared grid-row: 1 (text-roll.css), so painted output is byte-identical regardless of DOM/sibling order — only visible via DOM inspection mid-roll, never visually.

divergences: `bind:value` becomes the standard controlled/uncontrolled split: uncontrolled by default (`defaultValue` seeds it), controlled the moment a `value` prop is passed with `onValueChange`.
`class` becomes `className` (house-wide rename).
The Svelte source's autoResize `$effect` runs as `useIsomorphicLayoutEffect` keyed [autoResize, value, rows], so the height write lands before paint exactly as Svelte's pre-paint effect does.
`class` prop becomes `className`.
`done` snippet becomes a `done?: ReactNode` prop.
`ref = $bindable(null)` becomes `forwardRef<HTMLDivElement>`.

`useElapsed`'s server snapshot is a deterministic `0`, so a server-rendered ThinkingIndicator shows "0s"; Svelte's `createElapsed({ since })` seeds from the server's wall clock, which no hydration render can reproduce. The live duration arrives in the layout phase, before the first paint.

minors.problem: `showDone = !running && done !== undefined` was transposed literally, but `done` is now `ReactNode` rather than `Snippet`. A caller writing the idiomatic React `done={someCondition && …}` passes `false`, which is not `undefined`, so with `running={false}` the component renders an empty `.ft-thinking-done` span and suppresses the status label — where the Svelte side could only ever receive a snippet or `undefined`. A `!= null && done !== false` style guard (or documenting the edge in divergences) would close it.

divergences: `bind:activeId` becomes the standard controlled/uncontrolled split: `activeId` is controlled when passed (pair it with `onSelect` to move the highlight); omit it and the list owns its own selection, reporting every pick through `onSelect`.

A Svelte consumer passing a non-bound initial `activeId` and expecting clicks to still move the highlight must instead omit the prop (uncontrolled) or update it from `onSelect` — there is no defaultActiveId, matching the Tabs precedent.
Timestamps read `useNow()`'s shared module clock instead of a per-instance `createNow`; one interval per page, none under SSR.

SSR relative timestamps: Svelte's `createNow` seeds itself with `Date.now()` at construction, so its server HTML carries real relative labels. React's shared clock cannot — the hydration render has no way to reproduce the server's timestamp, and sampling the wall clock on a render path breaks convention C-7 — so `useNow()` returns a `NaN` sentinel until the clock is retained in the layout phase, and `formatRelativeTime` renders a non-finite `now` as `""`. The server HTML therefore ships an empty label (never a wrong one) and it fills in before the first paint. Pinned by `react/src/internals/use-elapsed.ssr.test.ts`.

minors.problem: Controlled/uncontrolled split diverges from Svelte's `$bindable` in one call shape: a Svelte consumer passing a non-bound `activeId` still gets the highlight moved on click (the component writes its local copy), whereas here passing `activeId` freezes the highlight unless the consumer feeds it back from `onSelect`. Disclosed by the port agent and consistent with the house precedent in react/src/components/tabs/Tabs.tsx (identical isControlled/uncontrolledValue shape), and the added test covers the uncontrolled half — acceptable, but it is a real API-surface difference worth recording in the component README.

divergences: `value` (`$bindable(null)`) becomes a controlled `value` prop plus `onValueChange`; the component keeps an internal copy re-synced during render when the caller changes the prop, so controlled and uncontrolled use both work off one implementation — there is no two-way binding.
`ref = $bindable(null)` on the trigger becomes `forwardRef<HTMLButtonElement, TimePickerProps>`; the exposed element is still the `<button>`.
`class` prop is spelled `className` (PORTING.md API contract).
D-2: `data-state` on the panel is an ordinary React attribute; `markSurfaceState` and the `onintrostart`/`onoutrostart` handlers are not ported. Same DOM output ("open" then "closing").

D-1: the panel is rendered into `document.body` with `createPortal` instead of a node moved by `use:portal`. Same resulting DOM, but synthetic React events from the panel still bubble through the React tree (inert here — dismissal listens natively on `document`).
`TIME_PICKER_KEY` (a `unique symbol`) becomes `TimePickerReactContext` + `useTimePickerContext` in `types.ts`; like the Svelte barrel, `index.ts` does not export it.

Open-time scroll: `tick().then(() => scrollActiveIntoView(index))` becomes a parked pending-index ref paid out by an effect keyed on `[panelNode, open]` (the panel mounts a commit later under presence, and a reopen can reuse the same node).
`TimePickerPanel`'s `class`/`ref` props survive as `className` + `forwardRef`, but the component is not exported from `index.ts` (matching the Svelte barrel).

Apart from the active-slot reconciliation recorded below, behaviourally unchanged elsewhere: reduced-motion fast path, the `anchored` transition, `data-side`/`data-align` and `transform-origin` — `data-align` stays the statically requested "start" while `data-side` is the resolved one, the same asymmetry the source ships.

React re-resolves the highlighted slot onto the same TIME when `step`, `min` or `max` change the grid (and therefore scrolls an open panel); the Svelte source keeps the raw numeric index, which can leave `aria-activedescendant` citing a removed row.

TimePicker formats its trigger and slot labels with Intl.DateTimeFormat and the runtime's default locale when `locale` is omitted, so a server render and its hydration can produce different text; pass an explicit `locale` for SSR-stable output.
`class` prop becomes `className` (standard port convention)
`content` snippet becomes a `content?: (item: TimelineItem) => ReactNode` render prop

The per-toast entrance and exit are owned by `<Toaster>`'s per-item presence clock rather than by `<Toast>` itself, so a `<Toast>` rendered directly outside a `<Toaster>` is static where the Svelte one still plays its 300 ms rise in and 200 ms sink out.

A dismissed toast is `inert` for the length of its exit (the presence clock's default), so its Retry and Dismiss buttons stop answering clicks and focus inside it is released; the Svelte toast root carries no `inert` and stays interactive until the outro destroys it.

pressed is React state seeded once from the `pressed` prop (mirrors Svelte's pressed = $bindable(false)), not a controlled/uncontrolled toggle via `pressed ?? state` — re-passing a different `pressed` value after mount does not resync it, matching the Svelte bindable-prop semantics exactly.

ToggleHarness.test.svelte (Svelte bind: rig) became ToggleHarness.tsx (not .test.tsx, so vitest's src/**/*.test.{ts,tsx} include does not collect it as its own empty suite); its assertions live in Toggle.test.tsx as before.

`value` is a controlled prop instead of a Svelte `$bindable`: pass `value` + `onValueChange` to control the selection; omit `value` entirely and the group keeps its own internal copy (seeded to "") and still reports every change through `onValueChange`. No `defaultValue` prop was added.

`TOGGLE_GROUP_KEY` is a `React.Context<ToggleGroupContext | undefined>` (displayName "ToggleGroupContext") rather than the Svelte `unique symbol` context key — read it with `useContext(TOGGLE_GROUP_KEY)`. Same exported name, same optional-read contract (an item outside a group gets `undefined`, never a throw). Mirrors the BUTTON_GROUP_CONTEXT_KEY precedent.

`ToggleGroupContext.focusedValue`, `.value`, `.type`, `.disabled`, `.size` and `.orientation` are plain readonly values, not Svelte getters; the root rebuilds the context object every render and that rebuild is what re-renders the items. `register`/`unregister` are the only identity-stable members — they appear in each item's effect dependency list, the React counterpart of the Svelte `untrack` guard against the register/unregister loop.
`class` becomes `className` on both parts. Neither part spreads rest props, matching the Svelte sources which read no `...restProps`.

The two Svelte `<style>` blocks split into two colocated stylesheets, `toggle-group.css` and `toggle-group-item.css` (one per Svelte file, per the sidebar precedent). Both are already anchored on the sources' own root classes `.ft-toggle-group` / `.ft-toggle-group-item`, so no port-added anchor class was needed; the `prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference` block and the `light-dark()` accent fallback are carried over verbatim.

Test transposition: the two `bind:value` round-trip tests become "round-trips a single/multiple selection through the value channel", asserting the same values via the harness's `onValueChange`; "binds the root element" becomes "exposes the root element through the ref" using `createRef` + `forwardRef`. `ToggleGroupHarness.test.svelte` is now an inline `Harness` component inside `ToggleGroup.test.tsx`. Every `await tick()` flush is dropped as Svelte-scheduler mechanics (RTL's `fireEvent` already acts).

A defined-but-falsy children (e.g. `{cond && <Icon/>}` collapsing to `false`, or an explicit `null`) renders nothing instead of falling back to the label/value text. `children != null` would be marginally closer to the Svelte truthiness check. Cosmetic: `undefined` is the only case the Svelte snippet channel can actually produce, and both the Svelte and React tests for the fallback pass.

divergences: `bind:open` becomes the standard controlled/uncontrolled split: `open` is uncontrolled by default (auto-open on failure still applies) and controlled when the prop is passed — pair it with `onToggle`; when controlled, a header click reports through `onToggle` but the parent owns the value.
Snippet props become render props: `input`/`output` are `(value: unknown) => ReactNode` receiving `call.input`/`call.output`; `icon` (parameterless snippet) is a plain `ReactNode`.

minors.problem: Line 251 renders `inert={!isOpen}` as a declarative boolean, which only react-dom 19 understands. The package peer range is `^18.0.0 || ^19.0.0`; on React 18 a boolean for an unrecognised attribute is dropped (with a dev warning), so on that major a collapsed card's payloads stay focusable and reachable by assistive tech — the Svelte source sets the attribute unconditionally. Every other component in the port (Presence/Dialog) sets `inert` imperatively, which works on both majors. Correct and tested under React 19.

divergences: Svelte's `item` Snippet<[ToolTimelineItemData, number]> prop becomes a render-prop function `(item, index) => ReactNode` per PORTING.md snippet-to-ReactNode mapping.
Svelte source has no rest-prop spread on the root div, so the React port matches it exactly (no ...rest) rather than adding one speculatively.

SSR relative timestamps: Svelte's `createNow` seeds itself with `Date.now()` at construction, so its server HTML carries real relative labels. React's shared clock cannot — the hydration render has no way to reproduce the server's timestamp, and sampling the wall clock on a render path breaks convention C-7 — so `useNow()` returns a `NaN` sentinel until the clock is retained in the layout phase, and `formatRelativeTime` renders a non-finite `now` as `""`. The server HTML therefore ships an empty label (never a wrong one) and it fills in before the first paint. Pinned by `react/src/internals/use-elapsed.ssr.test.ts`.

`class` prop becomes `className`; the bindable `ref` (trigger wrapper span) arrives via forwardRef per PORTING.md.
The dev-only focusable-trigger warning gates on `process.env.NODE_ENV !== "production"` instead of `import.meta.env.DEV` (same pattern as fluid-cursor/fireworks-hdr).

Trigger and bubble hover/focus listeners are attached natively via addEventListener (mirroring the source's imperative wiring and real pointerenter/pointerleave events) rather than React synthetic props — React's enter/leave plugin synthesises those from pointerover/out.
The in-only entrance is a bare `runTransition` in a layout effect (no `usePresence`): the source uses `in:anchored` with no outro, so close/unmount stays instant.
The bubble is rendered through the `Portal` component (createPortal) instead of the node-moving `use:portal` action — same resulting DOM under document.body (contract divergence D-1, inert here).

Per-frame spring values are written imperatively to the gradient node in the rAF loop (setAttribute "y1"/"y2") instead of round-tripping through state, so the component and its children never re-render during the animation; the rendered JSX keeps y1/y2 at their 0 seed, which is also what the server markup emits.

The SVG gradient id is minted per instance with useFancyId("tracing-beam-gradient") and referenced as url(#id), where the source hardcodes the id; the React side therefore supports several beams on one page.

TypingIndicatorProps extends HTMLAttributes<HTMLDivElement> and spreads ...rest onto the root div, so a consumer can pass id/onClick/data-* or override role/aria-live/style; the Svelte component declares a fixed prop list and spreads nothing.

`active` is no longer `bind:active`: it is the controlled/uncontrolled pair `active?: boolean` + `onActiveChange?: (active: boolean) => void` (added prop). The component keeps its own copy either way and re-syncs it in the render path when the prop changes, so every observable behaviour the Svelte tests assert is preserved — a supplied `active` opens/closes the panel, a button-driven change closes it even when `active` was passed and no callback is wired, and an externally driven change still fires no callback. Mirrors the Dialog/ApprovalCard convention already in the package.
`class` → `className` (PORTING.md).
The `ref = $bindable(null)` prop is gone; the root `HTMLDivElement` arrives through `forwardRef` (PORTING.md / C-4).

No `mounted` state: a React effect never runs on the server, and the canvas node arrives through `useElementRef`, which together give exactly the guarantee the Svelte flag existed for. Not consumer-visible.

No `untrack()` around the reduced-motion still frame and the ResizeObserver repaint — there is no reactivity graph to escape. The same guarantee (incoming `samples`/`demo` cannot restart the loop) comes from reading them through `useLiveRef` instead of effect dependencies. Effect deps are `[active, canvasEl, barHeight, color]`, matching the Svelte effect's tracked set exactly.

`samples` is a prop in React, so a consumer bridging a 60 Hz audio pipeline re-renders the component and reconciles the panel subtree once per frame; the Svelte source reads `samples` inside the untracked rAF callback and re-renders nothing. The rAF loop itself is unaffected — `samples` is read through a live ref, so the canvas effect never restarts.
